text:
Cole Sillinger was born in Columbus, drafted 12th overall by his hometown team in 2021, and at 23 is still working out what kind of player he is. He has four goals and nine points in 21 games and 50 hits, playing about 16 minutes a night.

Our numbers say he has been a bit unlucky and a bit outplayed. Columbus has scored about 4.3 fewer goals than its chances with him on the ice, which should turn, but the Blue Jackets also take only 46% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there (expected goals measure the quality of chances), three points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey had his results running ahead of his chances last season, with strong teammates flattering him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking sees nothing far from the typical forward yet. Our range has him around 16 goals. The physical game is there; the next step is tilting the ice.
